San Francisco Planning, Article 10 landmark designation: Landmark No. 181, San Francisco Lawn Bowling Clubhouse and Greens (ordinance, Planning Commission resolution and case report)
sources.label: SF Planning, landmark designation

historical_record.description: Designated San Francisco Landmark No. 181, San Francisco Lawn Bowling Clubhouse and Greens.

The first game was bowled here, on a green John McLaren had laid out in the west corner of the Recreation Grounds for a club organised by the St. Andrew's Society on October 7, with bowls brought from Scotland; on November 25 the San Francisco Scottish Bowling Club was formed, with McLaren as vice-president and James Rolph Jr., later mayor and governor, as treasurer — the oldest lawn bowling club in the United States, still on its first site.
The permanent green, now Green No. 1, was laid out and opened.
After the earthquake the Army under General Funston took over the green as a horse corral for a troop of cavalry quartered in Sharon Meadow; it was restored by April 1907.

A second green, laid out by the Park Commission for the Women's Golden Gate Lawn Bowling Club, formed the September before, opened for play; park maps long marked it the women's green. The two clubs merged in 1979.
The one-storey Edwardian clubhouse was built, the date from the club's minutes, with $1,000 the men's and women's clubs gave McLaren — "the House that Jack Built". An addition followed in 1971.
